description: Naive English plural: append "s" for every count except exactly 1, unless the word already ends in "s". This is NOT the same rule as french-plural — French keeps the singular below 2 ("1,5 carotte"), English pluralises everything except exactly 1 ("1.5 carrots"). Real plural forms belong in Knowledge; until they exist all clients must be wrong in exactly the same way, which is what these vectors enforce. Hand-authored: the sandbox stays French-only and has no English reference implementation to generate this from.
generatedBy: hand-authored — sandbox is out of scope, no reference implementation exists

cases.why: The baseline: exactly one stays singular, the one case where French and English agree.
THE key divergence from French: English pluralises below 2, unlike French's "1,5 carotte" — "1.5 carrots".
The other side of the same divergence: a fraction below one still pluralises in English, unlike French's "0,5 carotte".
The mainline case — French and English agree here too, just for a different reason (French's threshold is inclusive at 2; English's is "anything but 1").
Reachable from describeQuantity: 160 g of carrot is 2.2 items.
Invariable words must not gain a second s ("hummuss") — the English mirror of french-plural's "ananas" case.
